items.title: Gazette confirms revocation of 10 Negri Sembilan exco appointments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The revocation of the appointments of 10 Negeri Sembilan executive council members has been gazetted today. "The state executive councillors had taken and signed their oaths and pledges of allegiance before Tuanku Muhriz on Aug 7, 2026, before assuming their positions. They are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.

items.title: N. Sembilan Ruler formally revokes appointments of 10 exco members
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir has revoked the appointments of 10 state executive council members, according to a state government gazette. The gazette said Tuanku Muhriz withdrew his consent and cancelled their appointments after stating that they had breached their oath of loyalty. The 10 affected Exco members are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Haji Zaifulbahri Haji Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Haji Mohd Asna Haji Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.

items.title: IHH unit appeals RM5.3bil Japan claim ruling
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IHH Healthcare Bhd's subsidiary Northern TK Venture Pte Ltd (NTK) has appealed to the Tokyo High Court against a ruling dismissing its ¥200 billion (about RM5.3 billion) damages claim against Japanese pharmaceutical company Daiichi Sankyo Co Ltd. The dispute is linked to IHH's 2018 acquisition of a controlling stake in India's Fortis Healthcare Ltd, which subsequently became the subject of legal complications involving Daiichi Sankyo and the former Fortis promoters. The legal dispute dates back to Daiichi Sankyo's separate battle with former Fortis promoters Malvinder Mohan Singh and Shivinder Mohan Singh.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - September 24, 2026
items.summary: PN activities suspended The RoS has suspended all PN activities but stressed that its registration has not been cancelled. Royal dispute probed Police are investigating the Negri Sembilan royal dispute from all angles, says Home Minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. Tabung Haji ex-COO charged Former Tabung Haji COO Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani has claimed trial over RM302,499 in renovation costs.

items.title: Global bond rout rolls on, pushes 30-year US Treasury yields to highest since 2004
items.summary: LONDON: US 30-year borrowing costs hit their highest in over 20 years on Thursday, adding strain to the government's long-term finances, as investors upped the compensation they demand to hold bonds given strong economic growth and high energy prices. The yield on the 30-year US Treasury climbed to just over 5.44 per cent, its highest since 2004, as prices fell. Global bond yields jumped on Wednesday and Thursday after business activity data pointed to strong US growth and rising inflation pressures, stoking Federal Reserve rate-hike bets.

items.title: Russia says will 'consider' US G20 invitation for Putin
items.summary: MOSCOW: Russia said on Thursday it would consider an invitation from the US government for President Vladimir Putin to attend G20 summit in the United States in December. President Donald Trump has invited Putin to attend the summit of world leaders in Miami, a move announced earlier this week by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio after his meeting with Russia's top diplomat Sergei Lavrov. "No decision has yet been taken" on whether Putin will travel to Miami for the summit, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Thursday.

items.title: PMCK's Q1 earnings surge 245pct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PMCK Bhd's net profit more than tripled in the first quarter of financial year 2027 (Q1 FY27). The private healthcare services provider's net profit for the quarter ended July 31, 2026 rose 245 per cent to RM3.05 million from RM884,000 a year earlier. PMCK remains cautiously optimistic about the private healthcare industry.

items.title: Understand legal channels, seek accurate guidance - Raja Muda of Perlis
items.summary: The Raja Muda of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail, said the Legal Aid Department plays a vital role as a bridge between the community and the justice system. "The services help the public understand their rights, get guidance, and choose appropriate resolution channels," His Highness said when officiating the closing ceremony of the Perlis state-level Legal Aid Department Discourse "Yang Jauh Didekati, Yang Sulit Disantuni" 2026 at Felda Rimba Mas today. Meanwhile, the Raja Muda of Perlis said the discourse exposed participants to the latest service developments, including expanded legal aid in civil and Syariah matters, the Madani Mediation Centre, Legal Companion, and Public Defence.

items.title: High Court to rule Oct 23 on bid to stop RHB closing shipping firm’s accounts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The High Court here today fixed October 23 to rule on a shipping company’s bid to restrain RHB Bank Berhad from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit. He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care. In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company’s application for a full injunction.

items.title: Inta Bina lands RM221mil Klang job
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Inta Bina Group Bhd has clinched a RM221.08 million contract from Prisma Melody Sdn Bhd, for the main building works of Gravit8 Phase 4 (Novva) in Kota Bayuemas, Klang, Selangor. Inta Bina said it is the fourth project the company has undertaken with Mitraland, extending a business relationship that has spanned 14 years. It raises Inta Bina's new order book to about RM645 million from about RM424 million, providing greater earnings visibility as the construction group replenishes its project pipeline.

items.title: Fire at Poland Starlink station 'sabotage', says minister
items.summary: WARSAW: A fire broke out at a Starlink satellite communications station in central Poland overnight, the digital affairs minister said on Thursday, calling the blaze an act of "sabotage." "This act of sabotage was deliberately designed to disable the station ... disrupting internet access for various institutions, including the Ukrainian army," Krzysztof Gawkowski told Polish public broadcaster TVP Info, adding that the fire broke out late on Wednesday and that the station was still operational. The station, owned by state-owned telecommunications company Exatel, is used, among other things, to transmit internet traffic through Poland, including to Ukraine, according to the minister.

items.title: MACC and FBI reinforce cooperation to tackle corruption, cross-border crimes
items.summary: MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said this was among the matters discussed during a courtesy visit by an FBI delegation led by Law Enforcement Attaché Varinder Singh to the MACC headquarters today. Also present were MACC senior directors Datuk Y.S. Karunanithy (Special Operations Division), Datuk Saiful Ezral Arifin (Intelligence Division), and director Datuk Saiful Hazmi Mohd Saad (Legal and Prosecution Division), as well as FBI Assistant Law Enforcement Attaché Cody Kirk.

items.title: Infomina bags RM62.7mil tech contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Infomina Bhd has secured a RM62.65 million contract from a local financial institution to provide technology refresh, supply and maintenance services over 69 months. The scope also includes ongoing support and maintenance services throughout the contract period. Infomina chief executive officer-cum-managing director Yee Chee Meng said the contract reflected continued confidence in its ability to support critical technology environments.

items.title: Former Petronas manager met Petros official informally before interview - Witness
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Sessions Court today heard that former Petronas manager Mohd Khairul Akmal Mohd Jasni met informally with a senior official of Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) at the Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club (KLGCC), before a formal interview for a position at the company in 2024. The fifth prosecution witness, a former Petronas employee, said the meeting took place before Mohd Khairul Akmal's interview with Petros chief financial officer and chief executive officer, Mohd Azha Abdul Jalil and Datuk Janin Girie, respectively, at the company's office in Kuching, Sarawak. The witness said Khairul Akmal applied for the position of Head of Upstream Finance at Petros in 2024, while he was Manager of Business Planning Performance Review Upstream at Petronas.

items.title: Ringgit ends higher against major currencies, eases versus US dollar
items.summary: At 6pm, the ringgit decreased to 4.0840/0880 against the greenback from Wednesday's close of 4.0780/0825. "The recovery happened even though the US dollar remained strong, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) staying at around 101 points," he told Bernama. At the close, the ringgit traded higher against a basket of major currencies.

items.title: MACC, FBI step up cooperation to tackle corruption, cross-border crime, says chief commissioner
items.summary: MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said this was among the matters discussed during a courtesy visit by an FBI delegation led by Law Enforcement Attaché Varinder Singh to the MACC headquarters here today. Also present were MACC senior directors Datuk Y.S. Karunanithy (Special Operations Division), Datuk Saiful Ezral Arifin (Intelligence Division), and director Datuk Saiful Hazmi Mohd Saad (Legal and Prosecution Division), as well as FBI Assistant Law Enforcement Attaché Cody Kirk.

items.title: Experts call for skid tests after multiple riders fall on green-painted lane
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Road safety experts are calling for skid-resistance tests on the green-painted stretch of the Federal Highway motorcycle lane near Subang after a viral video showed multiple riders falling on the rain-soaked surface. Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research chairman Professor Dr Wong Shaw Voon told the New Straits Times he believed the painted surface was applied for a reason, suggesting the coating was likely intended to warn riders of an accident-prone zone. "It doesn't mean that having painted road surfaces is not good," Wong said, adding that engineering interventions could produce coloured surfaces with even better skid-resistant properties than regular asphalt.

items.title: Starbucks to close another 250 coffeehouses in North America
items.summary: NEW YORK: Starbucks will close 250 underperforming coffeehouses in North America, the company said in a regulatory filing on Thursday, as chief executive officer (CEO) Brian Niccol deepens his turnaround push to revive sales. The closures come a year after Starbucks shut down several underperforming stores in the region, including its iconic Seattle roastery, in a restructuring effort that was estimated to cost the company about US$1 billion. Niccol completed two years as CEO of Starbucks in September.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN to negotiate with other parties soon, says Ab Rauf
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 24 — Negotiations for cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and other parties for the 16th Melaka State Election are expected to be held soon, says Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Chief Minister, said the negotiations would begin as soon as he receives the green light from the top Umno and BN leadership. Ab Rauf said the 21 state seats won by BN in the 15th state election would form the basis of the coalition's negotiations.

items.title: Honda gives City a tech-driven refresh
items.summary: The refreshed sedan, marking 24 years of the City in Malaysia, comes in four variants - E, V, Petrol RS and e:HEV RS - priced from RM89,900 to RM111,900, excluding insurance. The new City gets a redesigned front grille, new long light bar headlights for RS variants and Bi-LED headlights as standard across the range. The e:HEV RS comes with Honda Malaysia's 10-year hybrid battery warranty with unlimited mileage.

items.title: Malaysia, China agree on proposed ECRL extension to Rantau Panjang, says Anwar
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Malaysia and China have agreed on the proposed extension of the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang, Kelantan, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said he also received positive feedback on the proposal during his discussions with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul. Also present at the press conference were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Transport Minister Anthony Loke, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, and Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad.

items.title: SLGC IPO oversubscribed 3.1 times ahead of ACE Market listing
items.summary: For the Malaysian public portion, which comprises 28 million new shares, SLGC received 4,647 applications for 113.70 million shares valued at RM31.8 million. Of these, the Bumiputera portion received 1,962 applications for 31.30 million shares, while the public portion received 2,685 applications for 82.39 million shares. Meanwhile, the 70.0 million new shares reserved for private placement to Bumiputera investors approved by the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry, as well as 5.0 million new shares and 63.0 million offer shares reserved for selected investors, including institutional shareholders, have also been fully placed.

items.title: Tengku Zafrul asks N. Sembilan MB to name who allegedly forced him to sign proclamation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has been urged to explain who allegedly forced him to sign the Instrument of Proclamation regarding the position of Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir on August 3. Senior Political Advisor to the Prime Minister Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz said the question remained unanswered despite Ismail issuing a seven-page statement on the issue. Tengku Zafrul asked in a Facebook post today.

items.title: Foreign funds return, but rotation points to caution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Foreign investors returned to Malaysian equities last week but the modest inflow masked a broader rotation away from rate-sensitive sectors and towards more defensive counters, according to Moomoo Malaysia. Foreign institutions were net buyers of RM127 million of Malaysian equities, ending six consecutive weeks of net selling. Financial services recorded the largest foreign outflow at RM309.7 million, followed by plantations at RM131.1 million, utilities at RM84.5 million and healthcare at RM84 million.

items.title: Former Petronas manager met Petros official before job interview, court told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The Sessions Court today heard that former Petronas manager Mohd Khairul Akmal Mohd Jasni met informally with a senior official of Petroleum Sarawak Berhad (Petros) at the Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club (KLGCC), before a formal interview for a position at the company in 2024. The fifth prosecution witness, a former Petronas employee, said the meeting took place before Mohd Khairul Akmal’s interview with Petros chief financial officer and chief executive officer, Mohd Azha Abdul Jalil and Datuk Janin Girie, respectively, at the company’s office in Kuching, Sarawak. The witness said Mohd Khairul Akmal applied for the position of Head of Upstream Finance at Petros in 2024, while he was Manager of Business Planning Performance Review Upstream at Petronas.

items.title: ICT Zone's Q2 earnings up 11pct on lower expenses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: ICT Zone Asia Bhd's net profit rose 11 per cent in the second quarter of financial year 2027 (Q2 FY27), supported by lower operating expenses. The net profit for the quarter ended July 31, 2026 rose to RM4.25 million from RM3.8 million a year ago, while revenue jumped 40 per cent to RM71.9 million from RM51 million. For the first half of FY27, ICT Zone's net profit rose 22 per cent to RM8.7 million from RM7 million, supported by an 85 per cent jump in revenue to RM172 million from RM92.9 million.

items.title: LB Group invests RM1bil in Kedah plant
items.summary: The project, undertaken through its Malaysian subsidiary LB Advanced Material Asia Sdn Bhd, will be developed on 24.3 hectares at the Gurun Heavy Industrial Park. Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) chief executive officer Datuk Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim Sikh Abdul Majid said the investment reflects confidence in Malaysia's industrial ecosystem and its potential as a regional manufacturing hub. Malaysia's strategic advantages, robust heavy industrial infrastructure and welcoming investment environment were key factors behind the investment, LB Advanced Material Asia director Liang Sun said.

items.title: Anwar’s elder brother Idrus Ibrahim dies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today shared the sad news of the death of his elder brother, Idrus Ibrahim. In a Facebook post, Anwar said he received the heartbreaking news while returning to Malaysia from a three-day working visit to China. The prime minister also prayed for the deceased to be forgiven for his shortcomings, showered with mercy and placed among Allah’s faithful servants who do good deeds.

items.title: Nine areas in Sarawak record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nine areas nationwide registered unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 6pm today, according to data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS). Eight other stations in the state also recorded unhealthy air quality levels. Meanwhile, 47 monitoring stations across the country recorded moderate air quality.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 24, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed lower for the second consecutive day as a renewed rise in oil prices and elevated global bond yields weighed on investor sentiment. The ringgit also weakened against the US dollar, slipping to 4.0790. Ethereum and Solana also retreated, ending at RM10,869 and RM462, respectively.

items.title: PM's elder brother Idrus Ibrahim dies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expressed his grief over the death of his elder brother Idrus Ibrahim today. "On my way back to Malaysia, I received the heartbreaking news that my brother, Idrus Ibrahim, has died. Anwar also expressed his gratitude for all the memories and kindness Idrus had left behind, saying they would remain etched in his family's memories and hearts.

items.title: Traffic cop suffers broken arm, leg after driver rams roadblock
items.summary: Ipoh police chief ACP Muhammad Najib Hamzah said police managed to arrest the 29-year-old man after his car skidded at the Taman Wing Onn traffic light junction. Upon arriving at the traffic light area near the Perak State Secretariat (SUK) Building, the driver entered the left lane before making a sudden U-turn and rammed into a traffic policeman. "The driver then fled towards Gunung Lang, and upon reaching the area near McDonald's Gunung Lang, the driver drove against the flow of traffic before his car skidded at the Taman Wing Onn traffic light junction," Najib said in a statement today.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia ends lower on rising oil prices, elevated bond yields
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended lower on Thursday, weighed down by moderate selling pressure interspersed with buying activity as renewed hikes in oil prices and elevated global bond yields dampened investor sentiment, said an analyst. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 4.12 points, or 0.24 per cent, to 1,672.31, from Wednesday's close of 1,676.43. Turnover widened to 3.32 billion units worth RM2.74 billion from 3.20 billion units valued at RM2.99 billion on Wednesday.

items.title: UUE wins RM29.8mil jobs in Singapore
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: UUE Holdings Bhd has secured four contracts worth a combined S$9.3 million (RM29.8 million) in Singapore, bringing its financial year-to-date contract wins to RM127.9 million. In a statement, the underground utilities engineering solutions provider said its subsidiary, Konnection Engineering Pte Ltd, secured the contracts from Hong Kong-listed Wee Guan Group. UUE managing director Datuk Dr Ting Kok Hwa said the contracts strengthen the company's presence in Singapore and Malaysia.

items.title: Man rams traffic policeman, injures him while fleeing Ipoh roadblock
items.summary: Ipoh District Police Chief ACP Muhammad Najib Hamzah said that during the 9.45am incident, police managed to arrest the 29-year-old man after his car skidded at the Taman Wing Onn traffic light junction. “Three traffic personnel then pursued the car. “The driver then fled towards Gunung Lang, and upon reaching the area near McDonald’s Gunung Lang, the driver drove against the flow of traffic before his car skidded at the Taman Wing Onn traffic light junction,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: A diplomatic split screen as Trump and Xi meet
items.summary: US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping will meet for the second time this year, hoping to keep the world's most consequential bilateral relationship steady as both leaders grapple with a host of domestic and global issues. The split-screen moment highlights an existential question for the UN: does the world body, established after the calamity of two world wars, still matter? While UN delegates discuss "multilateralism" and hold panels on the world's conflicts, Trump and Xi – what the US president calls the "G2" – will talk AI, trade and defence.

items.title: Trump to fete Xi with lavish White House welcome
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump will host Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the White House on Thursday for a day full of pageantry with one goal – keeping the fragile peace between the rival superpowers. Trump personally greeted Xi on the tarmac after his arrival on Wednesday, the first time in more than six decades that a US president has welcomed a foreign political leader at Joint Base Andrews near Washington. The program includes a military inspection in the Rose Garden – which Trump recently paved over – and a gift giving ceremony involving Trump's wife Melania and Xi's wife Peng Liyuan.

items.title: Former hockey player, 79, pushed into drain, ex-election candidate held
items.summary: Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said the incident occurred about 10.30am in front of a row of shops. "The suspect's actions were also captured by a closed-circuit television camera at the premises belonging to the victim's friend. "She also did not know the victim personally," he said.

items.title: PM: China assures protection for Malaysian MSMEs
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the assurance came following Malaysia's concerns over potential market dominance by foreign players, including those from China, which could impact local traders. He said the matter was raised during a bilateral meeting with Li Qiang, as well as in discussions with major Chinese enterprises, including Alibaba. Present were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Transport Minister Anthony Loke and Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad.

items.title: Rapid KL to offer free shuttle buses for Bahrain GP at Sepang
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 24 — Rapid KL, in collaboration with Sepang International Circuit (SIC), will provide free shuttle bus services in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the SIC from October 2-4. Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the special shuttle bus service to SIC would operate from three locations, namely the bus hub at Level 1 of the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 2, the Mitsui KLIA bus hub and De-Village, Persiaran Millenia 2, Bandar Baru Enstek. To complement the service, Rapid KL will also provide shuttle buses within the circuit to facilitate visitors’ movement to key locations.

items.title: PM Anwar: China visit yields RM28b in potential investments across high‑tech sectors
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Malaysia has secured more than RM28 billion in potential investments following trade talks with major Chinese industry players, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The high-impact investments span several strategic sectors, including semiconductor manufacturing, artificial intelligence, robotics, electric vehicles, biotechnology, and advanced medical devices. “Overall, these business meetings recorded potential investments valued at over RM28 billion,” said Anwar.

items.title: Air quality dips in Sarawak with nine areas unhealthy, Melaka also affected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — A total of nine areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 4pm today, with the Serian District Police Headquarters (IPD) recording the highest reading at 200. Meanwhile, 48 areas recorded moderate readings, including Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur (75); Keningau, Sabah (60); Seberang Perai, Penang (53); and Kota Bharu, Kelantan (52). Another 11 areas recorded good readings.

items.title: Emrail loses RM59m LRT3 bond suit, ordered to pay Kuwait Finance House RM39m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — In a double courtroom defeat for rail contractor Emrail Sdn Bhd, the High Court has dismissed its RM59.1 million lawsuit against Kuwait Finance House (M) Bhd (KFH) and ordered the company alongside three personal guarantors to pay the bank RM39.09 million. Justice Quay Chew Soon dismissed Emrail's claim over a disputed performance bond for the Light Rail Transit 3 (LRT3) development in its entirety and allowed KFH’s counterclaim in full, holding the contractor and its guarantors jointly and severally liable for the outstanding debt, FMT reported. The court further established that the specific performance bond template required by Emrail was never incorporated into the financing agreement with KFH.

items.title: MCMC backs police crackdown as Op Pedo nets 53 suspects, eight of them teens
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 24 — The collaboration between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) continues to be strengthened to combat the misuse of network services for the purpose of online child sexual exploitation. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC, as the technical agency, would continue to play an important role in assisting PDRM, especially the D11 Division (Sexual, Women and Child Investigation) of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), in tracking down those who misuse network services and subsequently bringing them to justice. Fahmi said the collaboration also involved technical and forensic aspects to assist PDRM investigations into online child sexual exploitation activities.

items.title: Sabah sees 10 million searches on Xiaohongshu as China tourism interest surges
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 24 — Sabah has recorded over 10 million searches on REDnote (Xiaohongshu), China’s leading social and lifestyle platform, signalling a massive surge in interest from Chinese travellers, said Datuk Jafry Ariffin The Sabah minister of tourism, culture and environment disclosed the figures following his visit to the REDnote office in Shanghai yesterday, noting that the high search volume underscores Sabah’s strong visibility in the Chinese market. “This is a very encouraging indication for Sabah. “China remains an important tourism market for Sabah.

items.title: Police announce staged KL diversions as Sunday Coway Run shuts 34 roads
items.summary: “The roads involved are Jalan Stadium, Jalan Maharajalela, Jalan Dewan Bahasa, Jalan Bukit Petaling, Jalan Bellamy, Jalan Hang Tuah, Jalan Hang Jebat, Jalan Sultan Ismail, Jalan Raja Chulan, Jalan Conlay and Jalan Kia Peng. “Also involved are Jalan Perak, Jalan P. Ramlee, Jalan Ampang, Jalan Raja Laut, Jalan Putra, Jalan Tun Ismail, Jalan Tunku, Jalan Langgak Tunku, Jalan Pinggiran Tunku, Jalan Girdle, Jalan Bukit Tunku and Jalan Sultan Salahuddin,” he said in a statement today. He said that other roads that would also be closed were Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar, Jalan Persiaran Sultan Salahuddin, Jalan Parlimen, Jalan Dato Onn, Bulatan Dato Onn, Jalan Kinabalu, Jalan Tun Perak, Jalan Pudu, Jalan Sultan, Jalan Petaling and Bulatan Merdeka.

items.title: Masidi confident Putrajaya will secure Sabah borders amid Balabac Strait concerns
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 24 — Sabah Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun is confident the federal government will safeguard the state's borders in the Balabac Strait, despite concerns surrounding a US-backed Philippine military facility in the region. Speaking to reporters after the Sabah Carbon Forum today, Masidi said that border security falls under the jurisdiction of Putrajaya. When asked if Sabah would see additional security reinforcements, Masidi replied, “All I can say is that I don’t think they will allow Sabah to go undefended.”

items.title: Father, teenage son held over Kuala Kangsar murder of woman with disabilities
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 24 — A father and son have been remanded for seven and two days respectively, starting today, to assist in the investigation of a murder case involving a woman with disabilities (PwD) in Kampung Cheh Kati, Kuala Kangsar, yesterday. Kuala Kangsar district police chief ACP Heisham Harun said the police received a report regarding the incident at 2.38pm after family members discovered the victim lying face down and unconscious. A woman was found dead in the living room of a house in Kampung Cheh Kati, Kuala Kangsar on September 23, 2026.

items.title: ‘Income first’: Economy Minister Akmal says Budget 2027 must deliver better wages for Malaysians
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 24 — Income and wages must remain a priority in the planning of Budget 2027, alongside efforts to strengthen the capabilities of local companies in high-growth, high-value (HGHV) industries. Akmal said the allocation to Penang for the development of the National Automation, Testing and Equipment (ATE) Campus in Batu Kawan was also part of the government’s efforts to strengthen local companies’ capabilities, thereby creating better job opportunities and more meaningful wages for Malaysians. Meanwhile, Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government would provide land in Batu Kawan for the development of the ATE campus.

items.title: Penang DVS probes case of dog allegedly dragged by motorcycle in Batu Lancang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 24 — The Penang Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) is investigating an incident involving two men who allegedly dragged a dog using a motorcycle in the Batu Lancang area here yesterday. Penang DVS director Dr Saira Banu Mohamed Rejab, when contacted, confirmed that it had received a report regarding the incident. “The Penang DVS is carrying out further investigations into the incident,” she said.

items.title: Hajiji: Sabah setting high standards to protect carbon credit reputation
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 24 — Sabah will not permit unvetted projects or speculative trading to undermine its emerging carbon market, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Panglima Hajiji Noor said today, insisting that strong regulatory standards are vital to secure long-term investor confidence. Hajiji warned that poorly structured initiatives, exaggerated climate claims, undervalued natural resources, and the exclusion of native indigenous communities would severely damage the credibility of Sabah’s carbon credits on the global stage. Hajiji highlighted that the forthcoming Sabah Climate Change and Carbon Governance Enactment 2025 will provide legal certainty by officially recognising the state government’s ownership of carbon rights, subject to statutory provisions.

items.title: Only RM6.7m recovered from RM2.97b scams, Lim Guan Eng demands urgent action
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 24 — Lim Guan Eng today urged Bank Negara to spearhead a “whole of government” crackdown on digital fraud, cyber theft and scams, warning that billions of ringgit in life savings are at risk. The Bagan MP said elected representatives nationwide have been swamped with complaints from victims, ranging from ordinary Malaysians to professionals such as doctors, engineers and lawyers. He said Bank Negara must lead a coordinated response involving all government departments to curb the surge in crime and protect the life savings of Malaysians.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB coy over coerced signing allegation, claims ‘overtaken by events’
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 24 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim dodged questions today regarding his police report over claims he was coerced into signing a proclamation on the position of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, claiming the matter has been “overtaken by events”. “Oh, that was a long time ago, overtaken by events. He subsequently lodged a formal police report on September 8 to trigger an official investigation into the alleged coercion.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB rejects Anwar’s ‘rude, uncivilised’ claim, says exco acted within role
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 24 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today rejected Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s description of his and the state executive council’s actions as “rude” and “uncivilised”, saying they had not made any decision to remove or appoint the Yang di-Pertuan Besar. Ismail, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, said the state executive council had instead discussed the state administration’s position on a proclamation presented as the decision of the four Undangs. “The state executive council discussed the state administration’s position on the proclamation presented as the decision of the four Undangs,” he said.

items.title: Pensioner who endured seven years of golf balls hitting his home finally wins RM100,000 from Jitra resort
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — A 61-year-old government pensioner has been awarded RM100,000 in damages after enduring nearly seven years of stray golf balls pelting his bungalow in Bandar Darulaman, Jitra. At the Alor Setar High Court, Judicial Commissioner Aimi Zaini Azhar ruled that golf course operator BDB Darulaman Golf & Resort Bhd and landowner BDB Land Sdn Bhd are jointly and severally liable for private nuisance, FMT reported. The court gave the defendants 60 days to heighten and extend safety netting near Hole 7, review tee markers and the line of play, install warning signs, and implement all measures necessary to stop golf balls from entering the property.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB says exco barred from Wisma Negeri, urges review of directive
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 24 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today said state executive councillors (exco) had been barred from entering their offices at Wisma Negeri and urged the relevant authorities to immediately review the directive. Ismail, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, said he had been informed that the exco members were not only prohibited from entering their respective offices, but were also prevented from carrying out their duties. Ismail said the directive was conveyed to the exco members verbally rather than in writing.

items.title: Batu Gajah council empowers community to tackle roaming livestock blamed for road accidents
items.summary: MDBG secretary Muazatul Adawiyah Muhammad said the initiative allowed appointed community agents to act under the Local Government Act 1976 (Act 171) and the MDBG Licensing of Livestock and Stray Animals By-Laws 2012. The initiative involves 16 representatives from the mukims of Tronoh, Lahat, Tanjung Tualang, Sungai Raya and Sungai Terap, who were appointed as MDBG Community Agents for Stray Animal Management. Muazatul said their appointments would be for one year, from October 1 this year until September 30, 2027, in line with the JPKK appointment period.

items.title: Cheras landslide displaces 80 residents; families wait on safety verdict before returning home
items.summary: Kajang Municipal Council (MPKj) Councillor for Zone 6 Tan Kah Hoe said observations and assessments by the relevant agencies, which began yesterday, continued today, with the full technical report expected to be ready within the next few days. The agencies involved include the Public Works Department (JKR), Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS), Minerals and Geoscience Department (JMG) and MPKj. “Block D remains without water supply, while restoring the supply to Block C is taking a little longer as the relevant authorities are identifying the route of the affected pipeline,” he said.

items.title: ‘Many flowers make spring’: Anwar affirms Malaysia open to China’s digital investment
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Malaysia will continue to be open to China’s investment in digital technology as well as cooperation, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Speaking at the 5th Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE) opening ceremony here Thursday, Anwar credited the Chinese government’s willingness to showcase and share technologies through various platforms. This applies well to the digital economy and (this is) why we will continue to open our economy to benefit digital investments and partnerships.

items.title: EC says 17 new Sarawak seats unlikely ready for next state election
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 24 — The 17 proposed new Sarawak state seats are unlikely to be in place for the next state election, Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said. He said the review of the electoral boundaries for the seats would take longer than February 2027, when the term of the Sarawak government expires. In July, the Sarawak Legislative Assembly passed the State Legislative Assembly (Composition of Members) Bill 2025 to add 17 new seats, bringing the total number of seats from 82 to 99.
